pronunciation.notes: In everyday speech the middle syllable is often dropped, giving two syllables: FAM-lee.

core_idea: A family is a group of people related to each other, and, in a wider sense, a group of animals, things, or words that belong together.

senses.definition: a group of people who are related to each other, especially parents and their children

examples.text: She comes from a large family.
The whole family gets together every summer.
examples.note: singular verb: the family as one unit

examples.text: My family are all early risers.
examples.note: British: a plural verb after family

examples.text: They want to start a family next year.

compare.note: a household is the people living in one house, whether or not they are related

senses.definition: all the people who are related to you, including grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins

examples.text: Ravi has family in three different countries.
We spent the holiday with family.

compare.note: a relative is one person in your family

adaptation.grammar: Uncountable in this sense, with no article: she has family abroad, not she has a family abroad, which would mean a husband or wife and children.

senses.definition: in science, a group of related kinds of animals or plants, or of languages, that come from the same ancestor

examples.text: Lions and house cats belong to the same family.
Tomatoes and potatoes are in the same plant family.
The two languages belong to one family.

compare.note: a species is one kind of animal or plant; a family contains many species

subsenses.definition: a group of things of the same kind, or made to go together

examples.text: The company sells a family of small electric cars.
All the letters in the font family share the same shapes.

phrases.definition: be passed from parents to children, so that many members of one family have it
phrases.explanation: Said of a quality, a talent, or an illness.

examples.text: Red hair runs in the family.
Heart trouble runs in her family, so she has regular checks.

word_family.note: not related in meaning today: familiar means well known

usage_note: Family can take a singular or a plural verb. The singular treats the family as one unit (my family is small; the family lives next door); the plural treats its members as separate people (my family are all coming). Plural agreement is mainly British; American English normally uses a singular verb: my family is all coming. The plural of the noun is families.

learner_errors.correct: There are four people in my family.
learner_errors.note: Say how many people are in your family, or we are a family of four.
A y after a consonant changes to ies in the plural.

adaptation.semantic: In everyday English, family most often means the parents and children who live together; the wider group of grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins is the extended family, or simply family used without an article. Languages that use one word mainly for the wider group should note this narrower everyday meaning.
adaptation.grammar: Countable: a family, two families. In American English a singular family normally takes a singular verb even when its members are meant: my family is all tall; British English often uses a plural verb. The uncountable use, with no article, means relatives: he has family abroad.
adaptation.culture: In English-speaking countries family usually means a small household of parents and children; adult children often live apart from their parents, and family members in the wider sense are called relatives. Family before a noun (family restaurant, family car) means suitable for parents with children.
adaptation.false_friends: In some languages the word that looks like familiar is an adjective meaning of the family, or a noun meaning a relative. English familiar means well known, and the adjective for the family is family itself, used before a noun: a family meal.
adaptation.pronunciation: Stress on the first syllable, FAM-uh-lee. In everyday speech the middle syllable often disappears, giving two syllables, FAM-lee; both are correct. The first vowel is the short a of cat.
